dimensions.reasons: The submitted storyboard render and Group A overview views clearly show the requested wind-turbine scene: a three-bladed horizontal-axis turbine on grass, dusk rural backdrop, airborne debris, and a low-angle camera. Group B's wind_turbine_drivetrain.png also supplies a recognizable mechanical drivetrain assembly.
issues: The modeled grass is visibly a finite rectangular patch bordered by a featureless gray strip in Group A wide views, rather than continuous open terrain.
The airborne particle effect reads more as scattered frozen flecks than a convincing falling-leaf-and-dust system.
The main nacelle exterior does not visibly communicate the requested internal mechanisms in the finished storyboard shot.

dimensions.reasons: The tower is planted on a circular foundation, the nacelle is seated on the tower, and the three blades visibly join at the hub in Group A views. The drivetrain components in Group B are generally mounted on a common structural beam above the tower.
issues: Several small white/gray cube-like objects in wide_front.png and wide_low_angle.png appear unsupported and have no clear purpose.
Some airborne fragments are oversized or block-like and do not convincingly read as gravity-driven leaves or dust.
The abrupt transition from the grass patch to the surrounding gray plane weakens the physical continuity of the site.

dimensions.reasons: The turbine has a clear modern wind-turbine silhouette: matte white tapered tower, rounded white nacelle, dark hub band, and three long tapered blades with visible red tip markings in Group A. Group B uses contrasting dark-gray machinery, shafts, collars, and a ribbed generator-like cylinder, making the drivetrain legible as an engineering assembly.
issues: The individual drivetrain roles are not fully distinguishable visually; the gearbox, brake, and generator are inferred from the generic box, discs, shafts, and ribbed cylinder.
Strong rotor blur and fading in several Group A views obscure the blade airfoil/edge definition.

dimensions.reasons: The Group B storyboard has a plausible dusk palette, depth-of-field treatment, and a readable sense of scale, while the rotor blur suggests operation. The turbine geometry itself is clean and recognizable.
issues: The sky is markedly overbright and low-contrast in wind_turbine_storyboard.png and several front-facing Group A views, washing out the rotor.
The grass ground, gray border, and photographic-looking distant landscape do not blend into a coherent continuous environment.
Leaves/debris vary implausibly in scale, including a conspicuously large leaf-shaped object at right in the storyboard render.

dimensions.reasons: The spatial organization is correct and easy to read: the tall tower rises from the grass, the nacelle sits atop it on a yaw-like bearing/support, and three blades radiate from the forward hub at approximately 120-degree spacing. Group A wide_back.png and wide_elevated.png clearly confirm the turbine's overall assembly.
issues: The isolated drivetrain presentation in wind_turbine_drivetrain.png is useful documentation but does not clearly establish that those parts are enclosed inside the finished nacelle.
The surrounding gray border interrupts the intended open-field setting.

dimensions.reasons: Across Group A full-turbine views, the rotor radius appears roughly half the hub-height tower length, a sensible visual match for an approximately 80 m hub height with 40 m blades. The nacelle, circular foundation, tower, and rotor have broadly credible relative sizes.
issues: The tower taper is very subtle at render distance, so the specified broad-base/narrow-top construction is not strongly communicated.
The visible foundation looks relatively thin and small for a large utility-scale turbine.
The oversized leaf/debris foreground particles weaken the scale cue.

dimensions.reasons: The white painted turbine surfaces, darker hub details, muted grass, and dark metallic drivetrain parts are distinct. The sunset/dusk illumination in Group B gives soft directional shading and a warm horizon, while the drivetrain image shows useful specular and ribbed mechanical detail.
issues: The very bright sky frequently clips or washes down contrast on the white blades and nacelle.
The exterior turbine material is somewhat uniformly matte and clean, with limited surface variation at close range.
The grass shader is visibly repetitive/flat and does not integrate with the distant field backdrop.

dimensions.reasons: The core requested visual inventory is present: tapered tower, foundation, nacelle, hub, three blades, grass setting, dusk background, debris particles, and rotor blur. Group B's drivetrain render visibly includes a large gearbox-like housing, multiple shafts/couplings, brake-like discs, and a ribbed generator-like unit.
issues: The gearbox, main shaft, high-speed shaft, generator, and brake are not individually identified or visibly housed within the normal nacelle render.
Dust is not clearly readable as a separate effect; most particles read as leaf-like flecks or miscellaneous specks.

No time-ordered animation frames are supplied, so the requested wind/turbulence-driven spinning rotor and gravity-driven particle behavior cannot be confirmed beyond the single-frame motion blur appearance.

criteria.criterion: The coherent horizontal-axis turbine uses the specified tapered tubular tower and principal dimensions.
The nacelle is genuinely configured as yaw-capable on the tower.
The nacelle contains every named internal machine arranged as one plausible drivetrain.
The hub carries the complete dimensioned three-blade rotor.
The completed authored scene has believable relative scale and consistently estimated unspecified dimensions.
The final render uses readable and believable material distinctions without prescribing unique materials for fixed object or effect classes.
criteria.evidence: In the author final image, the turbine reads as a smooth pale painted structure against a visibly mottled green ground surface, with dark/brown airborne debris and a softly colored cloudy sky backdrop. These surfaces are visually differentiated rather than rendered as one uniform treatment.

criteria.criterion: Enabled Wind and Turbulence fields participate in a functioning rotor-driving setup.
The atmospheric system produces distinct leaves and dust with the complete requested gravity, Wind, and Turbulence behavior.
The complete final lighting system combines a genuine dusk HDRI with exactly one contributing Sun lamp and visibly produces dusk illumination.
The selected storyboard render coherently presents the open-field turbine from the requested camera with effective depth of field and motion blur.
The requested final render and retained editable .blend form one valid Cycles-configured project outcome.

notes: This is a recognizable, broadly well-proportioned utility wind turbine with a successful low-angle dusk storyboard composition and an additional readable drivetrain study. Its main weaknesses are environmental continuity, washed-out blade/sky contrast, ambiguous internal drivetrain identification, and particle effects that do not convincingly demonstrate falling leaves and dust.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
